response:
It takes a lot of courage to share what you are going through, and it is completely understandable that dealing with incontinence is causing you so much anxiety and embarrassment. Please know that you are not alone in this; it is a very common condition, even though people rarely talk about it. The fear that others can see or smell your protective garments is a heavy burden, but often our anxiety magnifies these worries far beyond what anyone else actually notices. 

Because this is impacting your social life and intimacy so deeply, reaching out to a healthcare professional, like a urologist or a pelvic floor physical therapist, is a great next step. There are many treatments, exercises, and medications available that go beyond just managing the symptoms with garments. Additionally, speaking with a mental health counselor could help you navigate the anxiety and rebuild your confidence, so you can start feeling comfortable connecting with others again.
